result:
Done. Both gates pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 6 pass / 0 fail (the ValidationException stack trace in the output is pre-existing log noise from the `posts.search` starter test, not a failure).

I fixed the open redirect by adding a single validation point for user-supplied return paths in `app/Support/Redirects.ts`: `sanitizeRedirectPath(value)` returns the value only when it is a plain same-app path — it must start with a single `/`, must not be protocol-relative (`//…`), must contain no backslashes (browsers normalise `/\evil.example` to `//evil.example`) and no whitespace or control characters (browsers strip those before parsing), and it must still resolve to the same origin when parsed against a base URL; everything else, including absolute URLs with a scheme, bare hosts and `javascript:` values, yields `null`. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts` now runs both sources of the value through that guard: `show()` only carries a sanitised path into the Inertia form prop (so a hostile value never even reaches the browser), and `store()` picks the first of the validated body field or validated `redirect` query parameter, falling back to the unchanged `/dashboard` default — the authentication logic itself is untouched, so a correct password still signs the user in even when the redirect was rejected and a wrong password still fails with the same 422. Coverage lives in `tests/Redirects.test.ts` (the guard's accepted and rejected vectors) and `tests/controllers/LoginController.test.ts` (the `/login` page keeps `/posts/3/edit` and blanks the cross-origin variants); the latter also clears the pre-existing `guren check` warning about a missing LoginController test.
